newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Russia's U.N. cars said threatened by vandals.
newsitem.headline: Russia's U.N. cars said threatened by vandals.

text.p: Russia's U.N. mission said on Friday a note had been attached to many of its cars threatening to spray-paint the vehicles and let the air out of the tires if their drivers failed to comply with parking regulations.
"Pay for a garage like everybody else!" said the notice, signed by a group called East Side Neighbourhood Committee and shown to reporters by the Russian U.N. mission.
"Obey the law like everybody else! Don't tie up the parking spaces like everybody else!
"If you don't comply we will spray-paint your car and take the air out of your tires! (for starters...)," it added.
The Russian and Belarus U.N. missions are involved in a battle with New York city authorities over a fight between two of their diplomats and two policemen December 29.
The police said the diplomats attacked the officers after they were seen parked near a fire hydrant and were about to drive away apparently intoxicated.
The diplomats said they were attacked by the police who dragged them from the car and took them to a police station in handcuffs. One of them had his elbow dislocated and his glasses broken.

New York Mayor Rudolph Giuliani, who sided with the police, has accused the Russian and Belarus U.N. missions of failing to pay tens of thousands of dollars in parking fines. Diplomats are immune from prosecution.
The mayor's office said 150 cars belonging to the two missions racked up more than 15,000 parking tickets in the first half of 1996 alone.
The Russian mission has complained it is allotted only 10 parking spaces for more than 100 cars.
